terms.meaning: the first public page a new visitor sees
a profile of a kind of player or audience that the site describes
a named value in the stylesheet that can be reused in many places

sections.name: File setup, tint
sections.title: Imports and colour helper
sections.what: Brings in the page's building blocks: the graphic, the link tool, the landing copy, and the persona list. Also defines a helper that turns a named stylesheet colour into a style value for an element. Some imported names, such as IN_DEVELOPMENT and LIVE_NOW, are not used in the visible lines.
sections.why: Likely reason: the helper lets each element pick a colour from the stylesheet without repeating code.
sections.watch_out: The helper trusts that the name is a real stylesheet colour. A wrong name shows no colour and reports no error.

sections.name: Brand
sections.title: Logo and wordmark
sections.what: Draws the small five-bar mark followed by the words ALTER EGO. It is used in both the header and the footer so the brand looks the same in both places.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared component means the logo is edited in one place.
sections.watch_out: The mark is decorative and hidden from screen readers, so the written name is what carries the brand for assistive tools.

sections.name: Landing (part 1)
sections.title: Header, hero and persona strip
sections.what: Shows the top bar with the brand link, three jump links to page sections, and Sign in and Join free buttons. Below it is the headline, the lead paragraph about practising judgement, two calls to action, and a row of five persona tiles that link down to their roster cards.
sections.why: Likely reason: the first screen explains the product and invites visitors to join.
sections.watch_out: The jump links point to fixed section ids, so renaming an id silently breaks the link.

sections.name: Landing (part 2)
sections.title: Live now, roster and in-development lists
sections.what: Builds three blocks from content lists: Live now cards from LIVE_NOW, roster cards showing each analyst's sport, mentality and signature tool from PERSONA_SLUGS, PERSONAS and ROSTER_COPY, and numbered in-development steps from IN_DEVELOPMENT. The in-development section states that these are not available yet.
sections.why: Likely reason: the wording lives in content files so it can change without touching the layout.
sections.watch_out: The roster heading says five analysts as fixed text, so adding or removing a persona also means updating that sentence.

sections.name: Landing (part 3)
sections.title: Principles block and footer
sections.what: Shows the What we hold to cards from PRINCIPLES, then a footer with links to Terms, Privacy, Attributions and How AI is used, and a beta notice stating the analysts are AI characters with no link to any athlete, team or league.
sections.why: Likely reason: the footer carries the legal and disclaimer lines on every landing page.
sections.watch_out: The no-affiliation wording is fixed text here, and visitors may rely on it, so changes to it should be reviewed carefully.

summary: The public front page component that lays out the landing content, using copy and persona data from other files.
purpose: Introduces the product to new visitors.
why: Likely reason: the copy is kept in separate files so layout and wording can change apart.
how: Only the setup section of this file was visible. It imports the copy, the persona list, a graphic component and a link tool, and defines a helper that turns a named stylesheet colour into a style value. The steps that draw the page were not visible in this packet.
inputs: Copy and persona lists from the content and persona files.
outputs: The landing page layout, of which only the setup part was seen.
risks: The visitor's words come from the content file. The visible code shows no error handling for missing content.
debug: If the page is blank or missing a section, first check the content and persona imports, then the graphic component.
